# `silk/time/pattern`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Writes and reads dates and times with `strftime` patterns, such as `%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %z`.

## When to use

Use [`TimePattern`](#TimePattern) for a date format that is not ISO 8601: a log line, a file name, a date
in a form that a person typed, or the format of another program. For ISO 8601 text, the
`parse` and `Display` of the time types are shorter and faster.

## Details

A pattern is literal text and directives. A directive is `%`, optional flags, an optional
width, and one letter.

| Directive | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `%Y` | Year, four digits or more | `2026` |
| `%C` | Century, the year divided by 100 | `20` |
| `%y` | Year in the century, 00 to 99 | `26` |
| `%m` | Month, 01 to 12 | `11` |
| `%B`, `%b`, `%h` | English month name, full or three letters | `November`, `Nov` |
| `%d` | Day of the month, 01 to 31 | `09` |
| `%e` | Day of the month, padded with a space | ` 9` |
| `%j` | Day of the year, 001 to 366 | `323` |
| `%A`, `%a` | English weekday name, full or three letters | `Thursday`, `Thu` |
| `%u` | Weekday, 1 for Monday to 7 for Sunday | `4` |
| `%w` | Weekday, 0 for Sunday to 6 for Saturday | `4` |
| `%G`, `%g` | Year of the ISO 8601 week, whole or two digits | `2026`, `26` |
| `%V` | ISO 8601 week, 01 to 53 | `47` |
| `%U` | Week of the year with Sunday first, 00 to 53 | `46` |
| `%W` | Week of the year with Monday first, 00 to 53 | `46` |
| `%H` | Hour, 00 to 23 | `18` |
| `%k` | Hour, 0 to 23, padded with a space | `18` |
| `%I` | Hour of the 12-hour clock, 01 to 12 | `06` |
| `%l` | Hour of the 12-hour clock, padded with a space | ` 6` |
| `%p`, `%P` | `AM` or `PM`, and `am` or `pm` | `PM`, `pm` |
| `%M` | Minute, 00 to 59 | `36` |
| `%S` | Second, 00 to 59 | `22` |
| `%f` | Fraction of a second, without zeros at the end | `5` |
| `%N` | Fraction of a second, nine digits | `500000000` |
| `%z` | UTC offset; `%:z` has a colon, `%::z` has seconds | `+0100`, `+01:00` |
| `%Z` | Abbreviation of the time zone. It cannot be read. | `CET` |
| `%s` | Seconds from the Unix epoch | `1795109782` |
| `%F` | `%Y-%m-%d` | `2026-11-19` |
| `%T`, `%X` | `%H:%M:%S` | `18:36:22` |
| `%R` | `%H:%M` | `18:36` |
| `%D`, `%x` | `%m/%d/%y` | `11/19/26` |
| `%r` | `%I:%M:%S %p` | `06:36:22 PM` |
| `%c` | `%a %b %e %H:%M:%S %Y` | `Thu Nov 19 18:36:22 2026` |
| `%n`, `%t`, `%%` | A line feed, a tab, and `%` | |

The flags are `-` for no padding, `_` for padding with spaces, `0` for padding with zeros, and
`^` for upper case. A width, such as the `3` of `%3f`, sets the least number of characters,
and for `%f` and `%N` the exact number of digits. `%.f` writes a point and the fraction, and
nothing for a whole second.

A pattern that is a constant is checked when the program is compiled: an unknown directive, or
a directive that the value cannot supply, such as `%H` for a `PlainDate`, is a compile error.
The functions with `Dynamic` in the name take a pattern that is known only at run time and
report the same problems as a [`PatternError`](#PatternError).

A year before 0 has a minus sign before its digits, as in `-0044`, and a width counts the
sign.

Reading is lenient about digits and space: a number can have fewer digits than its width,
white space in the pattern matches any amount of white space, a directive that is padded
with spaces (`%e`, `%k`, `%l`, or the flag `_`) can have spaces before it, and names match in
any case, in the full or the short form. A year can have a sign, and then up to six digits.
`%z` reads `Z`, `+01`, `+0100`, `+01:00`, and the forms with seconds. The text must end where
the pattern ends.

A date is read from a year with a month and a day, a day of the year, or a week and a weekday.
A two-digit year without a century is from 1969 to 2068. A time of day needs an hour; the
minute and the second are 0 if the pattern has none.

## Gotchas

The names are English only. Names in other languages belong to a locale library.

## Examples

### Read a date and write it in another form

```silk
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.text.string { String }
import silk.time.pattern { TimePattern }
import silk.time.plain_date { PlainDate }
import silk.time.text { TimeParseError }

effect fn long(text: string) -> String ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  return match TimePattern.parse<PlainDate>("%d/%m/%Y", text) {
    Result<PlainDate, TimeParseError>.Success { value } => run TimePattern.format("%A, %B %-d, %Y", &value)
    Result<PlainDate, TimeParseError>.Failure {..} => run String.copy("not a date")
  }
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 ! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let written = run long("19/11/2026") |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  return if written.view() == "Thursday, November 19, 2026" { 0 } else { 1 }
}
```

Import as `TimePattern` with `import silk.time.pattern { TimePattern }`.

<a id="TimeFields"></a>

## `TimeFields`

```silk
pub struct TimeFields
```

The fields of a date and time that directives write.

### When to use

Return it from [`PatternSource.fields`](#PatternSource.fields) to make a type of your own writable with a pattern.
Fields that the type does not have can hold any value, because the directives that read them
are refused for the type.

<a id="ParsedFields"></a>

## `ParsedFields`

```silk
pub struct ParsedFields
```

What a pattern read from a text, before it becomes a value.

### When to use

Get it from [`TimePattern.parseFields`](#TimePattern.impl.parseFields) to read a text that has more than one value, such as a
local date and time with its offset, or to accept a text that can leave parts out.


<a id="ParsedFields.impl.offset"></a>

### Method `offset`

```silk
pub fn offset(self: &Self) -> Option<UtcOffset>
```

Returns the UTC offset that the text names, or `None` if the pattern has no `%z`.

<a id="ParsedFields.impl.date"></a>

### Method `date`

```silk
pub fn date(self: &Self) -> Result<PlainDate, TimeParseError>
```

Returns the date that the text names.

#### Details

The date is the year with the month and the day, or with the day of the year, or with a
week of `%U` or `%W` and a weekday, or the ISO 8601 week year with `%V` and a weekday. A
text with only `%s` gives the date in UTC.

#### Errors

- `TimeParseReason.MissingDate` if the pattern does not give a date.
- `TimeParseReason.OutOfRange` if the date does not exist, or a weekday in the text is not
  the weekday of the date.

<a id="ParsedFields.impl.time"></a>

### Method `time`

```silk
pub fn time(self: &Self) -> Result<PlainTime, TimeParseError>
```

Returns the time of day that the text names.

#### Details

The hour is `%H`, or `%I` with `%p`; `%I` without `%p` is before noon. The minute, the
second and the fraction are 0 if the pattern has none. A text with only `%s` gives the time
in UTC.

#### Errors

- `TimeParseReason.MissingTime` if the pattern does not give an hour.
- `TimeParseReason.OutOfRange` if the time does not exist, such as hour 24 or second 60.

<a id="ParsedFields.impl.dateTime"></a>

### Method `dateTime`

```silk
pub fn dateTime(self: &Self) -> Result<PlainDateTime, TimeParseError>
```

Returns the date and time that the text names. The time is midnight if the pattern has no
time of day.

#### Errors

- `TimeParseReason.MissingDate` if the pattern does not give a date.
- `TimeParseReason.OutOfRange` if the date or the time does not exist.

<a id="ParsedFields.impl.instant"></a>

### Method `instant`

```silk
pub fn instant(self: &Self) -> Result<Instant, TimeParseError>
```

Returns the instant that the text names: the seconds of `%s`, or the date and time at the
offset of `%z`.

#### Errors

- `TimeParseReason.MissingDate`, `MissingTime` or `MissingOffset` if the pattern does not
  give that part and has no `%s`.
- `TimeParseReason.OutOfRange` if the date or the time does not exist, or the instant is
  outside the range of `Instant`.

<a id="TimePattern.impl.write"></a>

### Associated function `write`

```silk
pub effect fn write<T: PatternSource>(static pattern: string<'static>, value: &T) -> ()
    ! WriterError
    ? &mut Writer
```

Writes `value` with the constant pattern `pattern` to the `Writer`.

#### Details

The pattern is checked when the program is compiled. A directive that is not known, or that
needs a part `value` does not have, is a compile error.

#### Errors

- `WriterError` if the `Writer` fails.

<a id="TimePattern.impl.format"></a>

### Associated function `format`

```silk

    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns `value` written with the constant pattern `pattern`.

#### Details

The pattern is checked when the program is compiled, as [`TimePattern.write`](#TimePattern.impl.write) checks it.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the text.

<a id="TimePattern.impl.parse"></a>

### Associated function `parse`

```silk
pub fn parse<T: PatternTarget>(static pattern: string<'static>, text: string) -> Result<T, TimeParseError>
```

Reads a `T` from `text` with the constant pattern `pattern`.

#### Details

The pattern is checked when the program is compiled. A directive that is not known, `%Z`,
or a pattern that does not give what `T` needs, such as a `PlainDate` without a year, is a
compile error.

#### Errors

- `TimeParseReason.UnexpectedEnd` or `UnexpectedCharacter` if `text` does not have the form
  of the pattern.
- `TimeParseReason.OutOfRange` if a field names no real value, such as month 13 or February
  30, or a weekday that is not the weekday of the date.

<a id="TimePattern.impl.parseFields"></a>

### Associated function `parseFields`

```silk
pub fn parseFields(static pattern: string<'static>, text: string) -> Result<ParsedFields, TimeParseError>
```

Reads the fields of `text` with the constant pattern `pattern`, without making a value.

#### When to use

Use it for a text that has more than one value, or parts that a single type does not hold,
and take the values with [`ParsedFields.date`](#ParsedFields.impl.date), [`ParsedFields.time`](#ParsedFields.impl.time) and the others.

#### Errors

- `TimeParseReason.UnexpectedEnd` or `UnexpectedCharacter` if `text` does not have the form
  of the pattern.
- `TimeParseReason.OutOfRange` if a field is outside its range, such as month 13.

```silk
pub fn parseFieldsDynamic(pattern: string, text: string) -> Result<Result<ParsedFields, TimeParseError>, PatternError>
```

Reads the fields of `text` with a pattern that is known only at run time.

#### Details

The outer `Result` fails for a pattern that cannot be used, and the inner one for a text
that does not have the form of the pattern.

#### Errors

- `PatternError` if a directive is malformed or unknown, or is `%Z`.
- `TimeParseError` in the inner `Result`, as [`TimePattern.parseFields`](#TimePattern.impl.parseFields) returns it.

<a id="TimePattern.impl.parseDynamic"></a>

### Associated function `parseDynamic`

```silk
pub fn parseDynamic<T: PatternTarget>(pattern: string, text: string) -> Result<Result<T, TimeParseError>, PatternError>
```

Reads a `T` from `text` with a pattern that is known only at run time.

#### Details

The outer `Result` fails for a pattern that cannot be used, and the inner one for a text
that does not have the form of the pattern.

#### Errors

- `PatternError` if a directive is malformed or unknown, or is `%Z`, or the pattern does
  not give what `T` needs.
- `TimeParseError` in the inner `Result`, as [`TimePattern.parse`](#TimePattern.impl.parse) returns it.
